topics.topic: A day on Venus is longer than its year; Venus spins backwards
Cleopatra lived closer in time to the Moon landing than to the Great Pyramid
The Zeigarnik effect: unfinished tasks are remembered better
Orionid meteor shower is dust from Halley's Comet (peaks Oct 21-22, ~66 km/s)
Octopuses have three hearts and blue copper-based blood; systemic heart stops when swimming
Astronauts grow up to 3% taller in space
First parachute jump: Garnerin, Paris, Oct 22 1797 (silk parachute from balloon)
Vampire bats regurgitate/share blood meals with hungry roostmates, incl. non-kin
Bananas are slightly radioactive (potassium-40, banana equivalent dose)
Mole Day (Oct 23, 6:02-6:02) and Avogadro's number 6.02x10^23; a mole of water is ~18 g
First jack-o'-lanterns were carved from turnips (Ireland/Scotland) and beets (England); pumpkins in America
Sugar-cube of neutron star weighs ~1 billion tons; ~20 km wide; spin hundreds of times/sec
First person over Niagara Falls in a barrel: Annie Edson Taylor, Oct 24 1901, her 63rd birthday (cat tested barrel first)
Owls can't move their tubular eyes; rotate heads ~270 degrees; 14 neck vertebrae vs 7 in humans
Clocks go back Oct 25 2026 in Europe (US Nov 1); Germany first nationwide DST in 1916 to save fuel in WWI; Franklin's 1784 joke essay
Statue of Liberty was originally shiny copper; unveiled Oct 28 1886; copper ~2 pennies thick; green patina from ~1903, fully green ~1920; 1906 paint plan dropped; patina protects
Félicette, first cat in space: Oct 18 1963, French Véronique rocket from Algeria, >150 km, ~5 min weightless, 13 min flight, recovered; statue 2019
Pumpkins are botanical berries (pepo) like watermelons/cucumbers; bananas, tomatoes are berries; strawberries/raspberries are not
Smallpox: only human disease eradicated; last natural case Ali Maow Maalin, Merca Somalia, rash Oct 26 1977; WHO certified eradication Oct 26 1979; he later volunteered for polio
Crows remember human faces (UW Seattle caveman-mask study, Marzluff); untrapped and young crows learned to scold; 20%->60% at one site after 5 years
Mars sunsets are blue (dust forward-scatters blue light); photographed by Curiosity/Opportunity; daytime sky butterscotch
NYC subway opened Oct 27 1904 (IRT, 9.1 mi, 28 stations, nickel fare); Mayor McClellan drove first train to 103rd St; 100k+ riders first evening
Wood frogs freeze solid in winter: up to 60% of body ice, heart/breathing stop, up to 7 months in Alaska, glucose antifreeze
Goosebumps: arrector pili muscles raise hairs; fur insulation/look bigger in animals; sympathetic (fight-or-flight) so emotions trigger it; likely evolutionary leftover in humans
First ARPANET message Oct 29 1969: UCLA (Charley Kline) to SRI, 'LOGIN' crashed after 'LO'; full login ~1 hour later
War of the Worlds radio broadcast Oct 30 1938 (Orson Welles): mass panic largely a newspaper myth; Hooper survey ~2% listening; most on Chase and Sanborn Hour
Skull-shaped asteroid 2015 TB145 flew by Oct 31 2015 at ~1.3 lunar distances, ~600 m wide, likely dead comet (Arecibo radar)

Houdini died Halloween Oct 31 1926 in Detroit (100th anniversary 2026); secret code 'Rosabelle... believe' with wife Bess; she held Halloween séances 10 years, last 1936 Knickerbocker Hotel rooftop; tradition continues
Mantis shrimp punch ~50 mph, <3 ms, up to 10,000 g; cavitation bubbles boil water, second impact, flashes of light; broke 1/4-inch aquarium glass (1998)
Saturn is the only planet less dense than water (~0.69 g/cm3); NASA 'float in a bathtub' joke; ~9x Earth's width; would fall apart (no solid surface)
Halloween is a cross-quarter day (midway between autumn equinox and winter solstice); Celtic Samhain 'summer's end', new year; true midpoint early Nov; Groundhog Day, May Day, Lammas
Bats aren't blind: all species can see; flying foxes rely on big eyes, many can't echolocate; microbats use vision for distant landmarks; some UV vision
Recreational fear sweet spot: Aarhus Univ (Andersen et al., Psychological Science) 110 people in Vejle Denmark haunted house; enjoyment and heart rate inverted-U
Candy corn: 1880s Philadelphia, credited to George Renninger (Wunderle Candy Co.); sold as 'Chicken Feed' with rooster box; made by hand; Halloween icon after late-1940s trick-or-treating
Apollo footprints on the Moon could last millions of years: no wind/rain, no volcanoes; only slow solar-particle wear or meteorite hit; 12 moonwalkers 1969-1972
Face pareidolia: Hadjikhani et al. 2009 NeuroReport MEG study, face-like objects activate fusiform face area at ~165 ms (faces ~130/170 ms); ordinary objects do not
Michelangelo painted the Sistine Chapel ceiling standing on scaffolding, not lying on his back (myth from 1965 film The Agony and the Ecstasy); 1508-1512; first shown to public Nov 1 1512
Koala fingerprints nearly indistinguishable from human prints (Henneberg, Adelaide, 1990s); only non-primates with them; convergent evolution; likely for gripping
HD 189733b: blue gas giant ~63 light-years away; blue likely from silicate (glass) particles; glass rain blown sideways by ~7000 km/h winds; >1000 C
ISS continuously occupied since Nov 2 2000 (Expedition 1: Shepherd, Gidzenko, Krikalev, ~4.5 months); 26 years in 2026; ~298 people from 26 countries; ~16 orbits/day
Tutankhamun tomb: first step found Nov 4 1922 as Carnarvon was about to stop funding; Carter 'wonderful things' Nov 26 1922; >5,000 objects; ~10 years to clear
Frequency illusion / Baader-Meinhof phenomenon: 1994 St. Paul Pioneer Press reader letter (Terry Mullen); Arnold Zwicky named it 2005; selective attention + confirmation bias
Sea otters have the densest fur of any animal: 500,000-1,000,000 hairs per sq inch (Seattle Aquarium); no blubber; eat ~25% of body weight daily

Sandwich named after John Montagu, 4th Earl of Sandwich; 1762 gaming-table story from a French travel book (likely apocryphal, Britannica); Cook named Sandwich Islands (Hawaii) 1778; National Sandwich Day Nov 3

Humans emit faint visible light (ultraweak photon emission): Kobayashi & Okamura 2009 PLoS ONE; ~1000x weaker than eye can detect; peak ~4pm, low ~10am; face brightest; metabolic free-radical reactions

Gunpowder Plot 1605: ~36 barrels under House of Lords; Monteagle letter; Fawkes caught near midnight 4-5 Nov with fuse and watch; Yeomen of the Guard ceremonially search cellars before State Opening; Bonfire Night Nov 5
Neptune completed its first orbit since discovery (Galle, Sept 23 1846) in July 2011; ~165-year orbit; ~30 AU (NASA)
You can't tickle yourself: cerebellum predicts and dampens self-produced touch (Blakemore, UCL); robot experiment, delay makes self-tickle feel more ticklish
Taurid meteor shower "Halloween fireballs": South Taurids peak Nov 5 2026, North Nov 12; Comet Encke (shortest orbit of major comets); slow, ~5/hr, larger debris makes fireballs (EarthSky, RMG)

X-rays discovered by Wilhelm Röntgen Nov 8 1895 (Würzburg); barium platinocyanide screen glowed; named X for unknown; wife's hand with ring X-ray Dec 22 1895; first Nobel Physics 1901; no patent (Britannica)

Wombats poop cubes: shape forms in the intestine (~10 m long) via stiff and flexible wall sections (Georgia Tech/Univ. Tasmania, Soft Matter 2021; 2019 Ig Nobel Physics); placed on rocks/logs to communicate

Marie Curie (born Nov 7 1867, Warsaw): first woman Nobel, only person to win in two sciences; radium-contaminated notebooks kept in lead-lined boxes at Bibliotheque nationale de France; Ra-226 half-life ~1600 yrs
Tardigrades survived 10 days exposed to open space on FOTON-M3 (Sept 2007; Jonsson et al., Current Biology 2008); revived, some laid eggs that hatched; tun state
Alaska is northernmost, westernmost and easternmost US state: Aleutians cross 180th meridian (Semisopochnoi Island in Eastern Hemisphere)
Pale Blue Dot: Voyager 1 photo Feb 14 1990 from ~6 billion km, Earth ~0.12 pixel; Carl Sagan (born Nov 9 1934) pushed for it
'Dr. Livingstone, I presume?' (Stanley, Ujiji, 1871) probably invented: Stanley's diary pages for the meeting torn out, Livingstone never mentioned it (Tim Jeal biography 2007)
Sharks are older than trees: earliest shark scales ~450 million years ago, first trees ~385 million years ago; sharks survived all five mass extinctions
Moon recedes ~3.8 cm/yr from Earth, measured by lunar laser ranging off Apollo retroreflectors; caused by tides (NASA)
First computer bug: moth found in Harvard Mark II relay Sept 9 1947, taped in logbook 'First actual case of bug being found'; logbook at Smithsonian NMAH (Britannica, NHHC)
A honey bee makes ~1/12 teaspoon of honey in its lifetime; summer workers live ~5-6 weeks (American Bee Journal, Kansas DOT Pollinator Partners)
Hedy Lamarr (born Nov 9 1914, Austria) + George Antheil: frequency-hopping patent US 2,292,387 (1942) to stop jamming of radio-controlled torpedoes; NIHF 2014
Voyager Golden Records: gold-plated copper, greetings in 55 languages, 115 images, music; committee chaired by Carl Sagan (born Nov 9 1934)
Spotlight effect: Gilovich, Medvec & Savitsky 2000 Cornell Barry Manilow T-shirt study, ~50% predicted vs ~25% noticed
Greenland shark: Nielsen et al. 2016 Science, eye-lens radiocarbon dating of 28 females; largest ~392 years estimated; longest-lived vertebrates; females mature ~150 years
France has the most time zones: 12 (13 with Antarctic claim) via overseas territories; Russia and USA 11 each
IKEA effect: Norton, Mochon, Ariely; subjects paid 63% more for self-assembled furniture; origami builders valued own work ~5x non-builders

Einstein-Szilard refrigerator: US patent 1,781,541 granted Nov 11 1930 (filed Dec 16 1927); no moving parts, heat-powered, ammonia/butane/water; inspired by Berlin family killed by fridge gas leak; Electrolux bought a patent; Freon made compressors safe; Oxford revival 2008

1833 Leonid meteor storm (Nov 12-13, North America, tens of thousands/hr, 'night the stars fell'); Denison Olmsted (Yale) found the radiant in Leo; Comet Tempel-Tuttle ~33 yr; ~71 km/s; 2026 peak ~Nov 17, ~10-15/hr

Doorway effect / location updating effect: Radvansky (Notre Dame) 2011, virtual and real rooms, more forgetting after doorways, returning didn't help; event boundaries; later studies: mainly under high memory load
Nellie Bly round-the-world trip: left Hoboken Nov 14 1889 (New York World), met Jules Verne in Amiens, rival Elizabeth Bisland (Cosmopolitan), bought a monkey, back Jan 25 1890; 72 days 6 h 11 min

More trees on Earth than stars in the Milky Way: Crowther et al. 2015 Nature ~3.04 trillion trees (~422/person, prior est. ~400 billion), ~15 billion cut/yr, ~46% fewer since civilization began; Milky Way ~100-400 billion stars

Axolotl regeneration: regrows limbs, heart, spinal cord, parts of brain without scarring; neoteny (feathery gills), lungs + skin breathing; up to 12 in, 10-15 yr; critically endangered, Xochimilco canals, ~50-1,000 left (IUCN via Nat Geo)

Apollo 12 struck by lightning twice (T+36.5 s, T+52 s) after launch Nov 14 1969; fuel cells offline, telemetry garbled; John Aaron 'SCE to AUX', Bean flipped switch; vehicle-triggered lightning; landed Nov 19, visited Surveyor 3 (NASA AFJ)

Flamingos are pink from carotenoids in algae/brine shrimp; chicks hatch white/gray; both parents make pink-red crop milk and can fade almost white by end of breeding season; feed head upside down; six species; colonies >1 million (Discover Wildlife, EarthSky)

Ben Franklin effect: Franklin borrowed a rare book from a rival in the Pennsylvania Assembly, became friends; Jecker & Landy 1969: students asked by researcher to return quiz winnings liked him most, intermediary (secretary) lowest; Niiya 2015 replication

Arecibo message: sent Nov 16 1974 at telescope upgrade ceremony, Frank Drake, 1,679 bits = 23x73 primes, ~3 min, 1 MW, 2380 MHz; numbers, elements of life, DNA, human, solar system, telescope; Sagan test; target M13 (>300,000 stars), arrives ~25,000 years (NatGeo, Icarus 1975)

Intel 4004 first commercial microprocessor: on sale Nov 15 1971, for Busicom 141-PF calculator; Hoff & Mazor cut 12 chips to 4; Faggin & Shima designed it, FF initials on die; 2,300 transistors, 740 kHz, 4-bit, 10 micrometre; adds two 8-digit numbers in 850 microseconds (Guinness, PC Gamer)

Suez Canal opened Nov 17 1869: work began Apr 25 1859 (~10 yrs), de Lesseps, forced labour/cholera, no locks (Napoleon's surveyors wrongly thought Red Sea higher), Empress Eugenie on L'Aigle, 164 km then ~193 km now, halved Britain-India trip, Ever Given Mar 23-29 2021, ~a tenth of world trade (History Hit, HISTORY, Wikipedia)

Lunokhod 1 first rover on another world: Luna 17 launched Nov 10, landed Nov 17 1970 Mare Imbrium; 8 wheels each with motor; solar lid, Po-210 heater; planned 3 lunar days, ran 11 (321 days); 10.54 km, >20,000 TV images, 206 panoramas, soil tests; French laser reflector, found by LRO 2010, APOLLO ~2,000 photons first try (Wikipedia, Guinness)

Gettysburg Address Nov 19 1863: cemetery dedication; Everett spoke ~2 hrs (~13,000 words), Lincoln 272 words ~2 min; photographers missed clean shot; envelope myth false; papers split on party lines; Everett letter next day 'two hours... two minutes'; 'world will little note'; five handwritten copies (HISTORY, Britannica, Ben's Guide)

Hummingbirds: heart >1,200 bpm, ~50 bpm in torpor at night; hover/fly backwards; Americas only, >300 species; bee hummingbird (Cuba) smallest bird ~2 g; ruby-throated nonstop Gulf of Mexico ~500 miles (search results: Smithsonian SERC, Audubon, Journey North)

First crewed hot air balloon flight Nov 21 1783: Pilatre de Rozier & Marquis d'Arlandes, ~25 min, ~5 miles over Paris; Montgolfier paper-maker brothers (Annonay), burned straw/wool/old shoes; Sept 19 1783 Versailles test with sheep, duck, rooster ~8 min ~2 miles before Louis XVI & Marie Antoinette; king wanted to send prisoners; Franklin witnessed; sparks risk (HISTORY, APS News)

Babies have ~275-300 bones vs 206 in adults: cartilage ossifies and bones fuse; skull several bones with fontanelles, close within 1-2 yrs, skull molds during birth; most fusion by puberty, collarbone early-mid 20s; bone living tissue; hands 27 + feet 26 each = 106, over half (Cleveland Clinic, Live Science, PopSci)

Mere exposure effect: Zajonc 1960s experiments (nonsense words, drawings, photos of faces, idiographs) rated more positively the more seen; Kunst-Wilson & Zajonc 1980 unrecognized flashed images still preferred; Goetzinger Oregon State black-bag student (hostile, curious, friendly); Bornstein 1989 meta-analysis 208 experiments; liking drops after too many repeats, songs (Wikipedia)

Day of Two Noons Nov 18 1883: towns set clocks by sun, noon signaled by ball drop/gong; 12:12 NY = 12:24 Boston = 11:17 Chicago; Dowd 1870 proposed zones 1 hr apart, Allen plan adopted; noon struck twice; NY noon ~3m58s earlier; Indianapolis Sentinel 'marry/die by railroad time'; Pittsburgh, Cleveland, Detroit refused; Standard Time Act 1918 (LOC blog, UPRR Museum, Untapped New York)

Wild turkeys: fly ~55 mph short distances, run ~25 mph, roost in trees climbing limb to limb; females fly/males run when threatened; winter flocks 200+; poults leave nest within 24 h; male head changes color red/white/blue; snood, 1997 study females prefer long snoods; gobble heard a mile+; 5,000-6,000 feathers; ~30,000 early 1900s to ~7 million; spiral (male) vs J-shaped (female) droppings (Smithsonian, PBS Nature, NWF)

Cocktail party effect: Colin Cherry 1953, air traffic controllers, dichotic listening/shadowing; little recalled from unattended ear but pitch/gender changes and own name noticed; attenuation idea; infants 5 months detect own name; works best binaurally, one-ear people more distracted; peaks young adulthood, older adults harder (Wikipedia)

Lucy fossil found Nov 24 1974 at Hadar, Ethiopia by Donald Johanson & Tom Gray; forearm bone in gully, then skull, femur, ribs, pelvis, jaw; named after 'Lucy in the Sky with Diamonds' played at camp; Australopithecus afarensis ~3.2 million yrs; 47 bones ~40% of skeleton; ~3.5 ft, 60-65 lb; small brain but bipedal knee/pelvis; National Museum of Ethiopia (Live Science, ASU IHO)

Uranus spins on its side: tilt ~97.8 deg vs Earth 23.5; year ~84 Earth yrs; hemispheres in long sunlight/darkness; day ~17 h; likely struck by Earth-size icy object; min -371 F; methane gives blue; Herschel 1781 thought comet; moons named for Shakespeare/Pope characters; only Voyager 2 visited Jan 24 1986 (Live Science, timeanddate)

Platypus fur glows blue-green under UV (Spaeth Anich et al., Mammalia 2020; Field Museum + Univ. Nebraska State Museum specimens); both sexes alike, purpose unknown; earlier glowing mammals opossums, flying squirrels (pink); lays eggs, venomous ankle spurs, no nipples (milk from belly pores), electrosensing bill, thick fur, nocturnal, eastern Australia (Live Science, Smithsonian, EarthSky/Wikipedia Monotreme)

First jukebox Nov 23 1889: Louis Glass & William Arnold, Palais Royale Saloon San Francisco; Edison electric (Class M) phonograph in oak cabinet + coin slot, 'nickel-in-the-slot', listening tubes, no speakers; one wax cylinder swapped by hand; ~25-lb battery; more in bars/restaurants/ferries; 1890 claim >$4,000; Gabel Automatic Entertainer 1906 24 songs; 'jukebox' from juke joints (Gullah 'rowdy'); ~750,000 US jukeboxes 1950s (Popular Mechanics, Wikipedia, Mystic Stamp, Wonderopolis)

Jupiter's Great Red Spot shrinking: ~41,000 km late 1800s (~3 Earths), 1.8 Earths at Voyager 1979, ~1.3 Earths (~16,000 km) by 2019; ~930 km/yr shrink from 2012; oval to circle; Juno >200 km deep; since at least 1800s, possibly 350+ yrs; cause and colour changes not understood (JPL 2019, Astronomy.com, Sky & Telescope)

Peak-end rule: Kahneman, Fredrickson, Schreiber & Redelmeier 1993 cold-water study (60 s at 14 C vs 60 s + 30 s warmed to 15 C; most chose to repeat longer); Fredrickson & Kahneman; duration neglect; Redelmeier colonoscopy trial with extra minutes, rated less unpleasant, more likely to return (Wikipedia, Colby cogblog)

On the Origin of Species published Nov 1859 (Darwin diary Nov 24, publisher records Nov 22), London, J. Murray; 1,250-copy first printing sold out in a day; 2nd ed 3,000 copies Jan 7 1860; full title '...Struggle for Life'; Beagle 1831 ~5 yrs; idea 1838 after Malthus; unpublished 1842/1844 sketches; Wallace letter 1858, joint Linnean Society reading; half of 'big book' done; only illustration tree diagram; Huxley defended; 250+ English editions, 29+ languages (Smithsonian Libraries, Lehigh, Univ. Missouri, EBSCO)

NASA InSight landed Nov 26 2018, Elysium Planitia near equator; entry ~12,300 mph, heat shield ~2,700 F, slowed to ~5 mph; 'seven minutes of terror'; MarCO cubesats relayed; CNES-provided SEIS; first marsquake Apr 2019; 1,313 marsquakes by May 2022; largest May 4 2022 ~magnitude 5; molten core ~half Earth's core size; HP3 mole stuck ~35-40 cm; dust on panels, mission ended Dec 2022 after ~4 yrs (collectSPACE, Astronomy.com, Space.com, Smithsonian, Wikipedia mirror)

Contagious yawning: ~half of adults catch yawns; triggered by seeing/hearing/thinking; Duke study 222 of 328; family>friends>strangers (Norscia & Palagi 2011) but empathy link not always replicated; kids ~4+; chimps and dogs; Nottingham 2017 Current Biology (Jackson) told not to yawn didn't reduce yawns, motor cortex excitability; brain-cooling (Gallup), more yawns ~20 C; yawning in womb; cause unknown (Psychology Today, PopSci, Big Think, Sleep.com, PsyBlog)

Hubble showed Andromeda is a separate galaxy: Cepheid spotted Oct 1923 with 100-inch Hooker (Mt Wilson), 'VAR!'; Leavitt period-luminosity; est. ~900,000 ly (modern ~2.5M); NYT Nov 23 1924; Shapley-Curtis 1920 debate; up to several trillion galaxies

Fibonacci Day Nov 23 (1,1,2,3): sunflower 55/34 spirals, pinecones/pineapples 8/13, golden angle ~137.5 deg, ratio -> 1.618; Leonardo of Pisa, Liber Abaci 1202 rabbit puzzle; known earlier in India; 657-sunflower study found exceptions

Butterflies taste with their feet (tarsal chemoreceptors); females drum leaves to test host plants before egg-laying; coiled proboscis, newly emerged join two halves; antennae smell pheromones; males puddle for sodium; land on people for sweat salt; moths/flies also leg tasters

Alfred Nobel's will signed Nov 27 1895 at the Swedish-Norwegian Club, Paris (<1,000 handwritten words), most of fortune to 5 prizes (physics, chemistry, medicine, literature, peace); premature 'merchant of death' obituary story after brother Ludvig died 1888 (no original copy found, may be myth); dynamite 1867, 355 patents; relatives challenged will, ~5 yrs to set up foundation; died Dec 10 1896, first prizes 1901 (HISTORY, LOC)

Mariner 4: launched Nov 28 1964 (Mariner 3 failed Nov 5, shroud didn't jettison), 228-day cruise, flyby Jul 14-15 1965 at ~6,118 mi, 22 photos on tape, 8 1/3 bits/s, ~10 h per image; JPL telecom staff hand-colored first image from printed number strips with pastels, framed for director Pickering; moon-like craters, surface pressure ~1% of Earth's (JPL, NASA History, Space.com, Caltech)

Dolphins sleep with half the brain (unihemispheric slow-wave sleep), opposite eye closed; ~4 h SWS per hemisphere per day (bottlenose), episodes ~40 min avg; float/log or swim slowly, captive ones on pool bottom; seen in calf a few weeks old; fur seals in water; frigatebirds sleep in flight (Rattenborg 2016); mallards at group edge watch outward (SciAm, Live Science, Lyamin 2008 review)
